subject: Clarify metering window and VAT offset on July invoice
messages:
From: Amelia Torres <amelia@stellaris.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@stellaris.ai
Date: 2026-07-19T08:12:00+01:00
Subject: Discrepancy on July usage invoice: metering window cut and VAT offset

Hi Lauren,

Hope you’re well. We reviewed the July invoice and noticed two items that don’t match our expected usage billing:

- An overage line for 'gen-inference' tokens that appears roughly ~18k tokens higher than our internal telemetry for the same period.
- VAT on a one-off credit that we negotiated in June doesn't appear to have been offset correctly — the credit amount shows up on the invoice but the VAT calculation still charged tax on the pre-credit total.

We run our systems on CET and our contract lists the billing aggregation window as 12:00 CET (noon) to 12:00 CET. Looking at the timestamps in the CSV export attached, it looks like the metering cut may have been applied at 00:00 UTC which shifted some of our sustained bursts into the next day and inflated the peak buckets.

Can you please:
1) Provide the raw metering aggregation window used for our July invoice and the per-day rollups for the affected days (July 8–12).
2) Confirm whether credits were applied before VAT calculation or after (and if after, provide the VAT delta and proposed remediation).

Attached: July_invoice_line_items.csv and a screenshot of the spike.

We’re being asked by our finance team for an explanation and timetable for any correction. Thanks in advance — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Amelia Torres
Head of Platform Ops, Stellaris AI
amelia@stellaris.ai

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T10:02:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on July usage invoice: metering window cut and VAT offset

Lauren / Rachel — quick summary from platform side after running the July aggregation job and VAT pipeline replays: 

- Root cause #1: On 2026-07-01 a pilot configuration change was rolled to the EU aggregation service that unintentionally moved the default rollup boundary from 12:00 CET to 00:00 UTC for a subset of customers. That change affected customers with non-UTC contracts (Stellaris included) and caused cross-day bursts to be assigned to the wrong bucket. The delta for Stellaris across July 8–12 is +18,146 tokens on gen-inference and +2,009 tokens on embed-search.

- Root cause #2: The credit-application step in the invoice pipeline is currently executed after VAT calculation for legacy credit lines flagged as 'post-sale adjustment'. For recent credit types we implemented last quarter the order was correct, but some manual credits (your June negotiated credit) still follow the old path. As a result VAT was calculated on the gross amount and then credit applied — VAT on the credited portion was not rebated.

Proposed remediation:
1) Issue a corrective invoice that shifts the metering buckets to the configured 12:00 CET boundary for the July billing period. This reduces the token total by 20,155 tokens (combined) for the affected days.
2) Recalculate VAT with credits applied pre-VAT and issue a VAT-offset credit for the delta: EUR 2,480.30.
3) Apply a one-time goodwill credit of EUR 250 for the operational friction.

Attachments: metering_delta_report.pdf (detailed deltas), vat_recalc.xlsx (line-item VAT diff).

Lauren — if you want I can create the corrected invoice and credit note drafts; Rachel can route through finance for approval.

— Marcus
Senior Billing Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

[attachment: metering_delta_report.pdf (pdf)]
[attachment: vat_recalc.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia@stellaris.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, billing@stellaris.ai
Date: 2026-07-22T08:05:00+01:00
Subject: Resolution: corrected invoice and VAT offset credit issued

Hi Amelia — thanks again for flagging this and for your patience while we investigated. Short summary and next steps below.

What happened:
- A configuration change in our EU metering service changed the aggregation boundary for a pilot cohort; that caused token counts to shift across days for July 8–12.
- The June credit you received was classified as a post-sale manual adjustment and (incorrectly) applied after VAT calculation in the invoice pipeline, so VAT on the credited portion was not rebated.

What we did:
- We generated a corrected invoice that uses your contract's 12:00 CET aggregation window for July. The corrected invoice reduces your usage by 20,155 tokens and updates line items accordingly.
- We recalculated VAT with credits applied pre-VAT and issued a VAT-offset credit of EUR 2,480.30.
- We added a one-time goodwill credit of EUR 250 to the account.
- Total credit applied: EUR 2,730.30.

Next steps and timeline:
- Updated invoice and credit note have been posted here: https://redwood-internal.svc/drive/finance/stellaris/updated-invoice-2026-07.pdf (also attached).
- Your account has the credit balance applied; if you prefer a refund rather than account credit, our billing team can issue that within 5–7 business days once you confirm.
- We’ll follow up with a short post-mortem on the metering pilot to prevent recurrence.

Please reply to confirm you accept the corrected invoice and how you’d like the credit handled (refund vs account credit). If you'd like a quick call to walk through the line items I’m available tomorrow at 10:00–11:00 CET.

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate you calling it out.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive (Sales Operations)
Redwood Inference
